content.summary: Resume the repaired live pilot under the user's instruction 'you have 100 tests. continue', interpreted as a ceiling of one hundred total live invocations including the twelve already consumed. Retain the prior failures and unchanged two-circular criteria. The remaining allowance is sufficient for the two bounded six-call cases.
findings: Skeptical baseline audit: this is engineering acceptance of source-driven search on retained development circulars, not a held-out legal-accuracy study or a ranking of BFS against UCT.

The same acceptance requires all three initial roles, at least two commitments, an accepted child, an isolated reconstruction, Java checks and a blocked meaning report on each source. Neither a model vote nor the call budget grants release authority.
The prior output-reference defect and integrity repairs passed the 277-test P6 regression. No generator, search or compiler code is changed for this resumption.

The former supervisor timeout of 1800 seconds was shorter than two 1200-second investigation deadlines. Increase only that outer timeout to 2700; retain per-call and per-run limits so a complete valid pilot is not interrupted by a mismatched harness limit.

The allowance is raised with structured JSON and a receipt containing the prior reservation-list hash. No reservation is deleted or refunded. The live pilot checks ledger and reviewed-plan ceilings before dispatch.

Expected model uncertainty remains reportable. A malformed response triggers the existing counted correction; uncorrected output or an incomplete branch/reconstruction fails the case. Inspect the actual source-backed differences after execution.
changes: Record user authorization for a maximum of 100 total invocations, preserving the original twelve reservations
Derive the supervisor allowance description from the reviewed plan instead of a stale literal
Align the outer supervisor timeout with both bounded cases
regression: Validate plan/ledger ceiling equality and unchanged prior reservation hash
Execute the two-circular live acceptance with retained requests, responses, usage and archives
